TESTIMONY OF
Deirdre Gilbert
Department of Marine Resources
The Department of Marine Resources (DMR) is testifying
In Support of
LD 1708 An Act to Create the Commercial Fishing Safety Fund to Further Develop Training and Provide Equipment to Recover Ships and Other Watercraft and Persons in Distress or Lost at Sea
Before the Committee on Marine Resources Sponsored by Representative Strout Date of Hearing: April 24, 2025
Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members ofthe Joint Standing Committee on Marine
Resources, my name is Deirdre Gilbert, Director of State Marine Policy for DMR and I am testifying on
behalf of the Department in support of LD 1708.
We understand that the recent, tragic loss of F/V Sudden Impact and crew members Chester and
Aaron Barrett is the impetus for Representative Strout advancing this legislation. The Department is supportive of efforts to improve safety in the commercial fishing industry and currently relies upon the Commercial Fishing Vessel Safety Council for information and advice on fishing safety issues. LD 1708
would create a new dedicated fund that could receive donations from any source and would be used
to support activities related to improving safety in the commercial fishing industry and improving the department's ability to conduct search and rescue and recovery operations, including the acquisition of necessary equipment. The Commercial Fishing Vessel Safety Council would advise on any expenditures from the Fund.
In the aftermath of a loss such as the Barrett family has experienced, it is important to find ways that positive change can be possible. For this reason, the Department supports LD 1708.
Thank you for your consideration and l would be happy to answer any questions you may have.

The Honorable Denise Tepler, Senate Chair The Honorable Allison Hepler, House Chair Joint Standing Committee on Marine Resources Cross Building, Room 202 Augusta, ME. 04333
Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, Honorable members of the Joint Committee on Marine Resources:
My name is Elizabeth (Liz) Michaud. I was born, raised, and educated in Maine. I am currently a part-time resident of Lubec, Maine and the president of the pending Maine non-profit organization, Green and White Hope, Inc. Most importantly for this committee, I am the aunt of Tylar Michaud, the 18-year-old fisherman who was lost while lobster fishing off Petit Manan on 21 July 2023. Tylar's buoy's were green and white and this nonprofit is my way of turning a tragedy into a movement that aims to bring every fisherman home. Green and White Hope's mission is to prevent fatalities among commercial fishermen through safety programs and technology advancement, while also advancing recovery capabilities in support of our Maine communities that rely on the sea; so it likely comes as no surprise that I am before you today in support of LD1708, An Act to Create the Commercial Fishing Safety Fund to Further Develop Training and Provide Equipment to Recover Ships and Other Watercraft.
From personal experience, the Maine Department of Marine Resources, and specifically the Maine Marine Patrol, was outstanding in support of our family while we combed the shoreline and searched from air and sea, along with the fishing community, across 30 calendar days. Their dedication and perseverance was without question. Unfortunately, in the community's eagerness to help (they had positive intentions, we are sooo grateful for them), Tylar's traps and boat had been moved and threw off the DMR's ability to accurately triangulate his last known location. This undoubtedly extended any timeline of us finding or recovering him. 30 days was agony, but we were blessed to finally find him, others are not so lucky.

I share this as an example of where additional funding could be used to ensure there is well understood command and control and a series of actions to be taken, and potentially drilled in each Maine harbor, so that our community resources can be used most effectively in search, rescue, and recovery missions. It is a well understood fact that the Coast Guard will never reach most of the state of Maine harbors with their cutters or aircraft until it's too late. They encourage the community to be educated and ready to save each other and that is hard to do with the limited funding that the DMR currently has available to address commercial safety education and capabilities.
In my role establishing this new non-profit, I can also testify to the incredibly dedicated people across the state of Maine and beyond, committed to advancing commercial fishing safety; The Maine Center for Coastal Fisheries, Maine Coast Fisherman's Association, Fishing Partnership Support Services, McMillian Survival Training, REDDE, etc. etc. There are 10's of people to address 1000's of fisherman and their families on commercial fishing safety topics. That is not enough and sadly their efforts (education, PFD distribution, etc.) are at risk due to the governmental changes. We are more and more on our own to protect and bring our fisherman home. Commercial fishing is the 2nd most dangerous profession, next only to logging, and there is a sense among the community that the risks will rise as more and more commercial fisherman decide to fish alone to improve their economics. Fishing alone also has some unique traits that require education that currently doesn't exist, if it did, it may have saved Tylar's life.
LD1708 can't promise to address all the issues across commercial fishing safety, but it will make a statement that the issue is important and provide an avenue for the department to receive dedicated funds to fill gaps in education and equipment that the State funding can't address in these times. I commend Representative Strout and Senator Moore for bringing this forward and encourage the support of the committee. Thank you for your time today and for the important work you're doing to preserve our fisheries and fisherman in the great state of Maine.
Respectfully submitted
Elizabeth (Liz) Michaud
President and Founder Green and White Hope, Inc (pending legal incorporation)

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Marine Resources

Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and esteemed colleagues of the Marine Resources
Committee, my name is Representative Holly Eaton, and I represent House District 15 ---- a
district of fishing and island communities including Deer Isle, Stonington, Brooklin, Tremont, Southwest Harbor, Frenchboro, Swan's Island, Isle au Haut, and Vinalhaven. These are places
where fishing isn't just ajob -- it's how we feed our families, raise our kids and hold our
communities together.
I want to thank Representative Strout for submitting this very important and thoughtful bill. LD
1708 speaks to something every one of us on the coast knows too well: the risks our fishermen
face every time they leave the dock. We have all felt the loss when someone doesn't come back.
Throughout this session, we' ve heard testimony again and again about the realities of working on
the water ---- not just the dangers, but the isolation. We've heard about the difficulty of keeping and retaining crew, the increasing pressure on captains to fish alone, and the deep concern that if
something goes wrong out there, there may be no one there to help.
This bill is a meaningfiil and necessary step forward. It creates a dedicated Commercial Fishing Safety Fund to help support both training and equipment that could save lives ---- not just for fishermen, but for those involved in search and recovery efforts. It would allow the Department of Marine Resources to better respond when things go wrong, while also helping fishermen better prepare and protect themselves before they ever leave shore.
I also appreciate that this bill includes a requirement to consult with the Commercial Fishing
Safety Council, ensuring that those with direct experience -- those who've lived these emergencies -- have a say in how the funds are used.
And as this committee considers the bill, I ask that we keep in mind our owner-operator model here in Maine. This isn't about large versus small operations ---- we are all independent. And that independence, while a source of pride, can also mean limited access to resources, training, or

Testimony In Support of

LD 1708 -An Act to Create the Commercial Fishing Safety Fund to Further Develop Training and Provide Equipment to Recover Ships and Other Watercraft and Persons in Distress or Lost at Sea

Good afternoon, Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler and distinguished members of the Marine Resource Committee.
i am Representative Tiffany Strout from Harrington, representing the towns of Milbridge, Harrington, Columbia, Columbia
Falls, Centerville, Addison, Jonesport, Beais, Jonesboro, Roque Bluffs, Whitneyville and Machias in beautiful Washington
County. l am here today to present my bill LD 1708 -- An Act to Create the Commercial Fishing Safety Fund to
Further Develop Training and Provide Equipment to Recover Ships and Other Watercraft and Persons in Distress or Lost at Sea.
Mainers have great love and respect for our fishing heritage and the communities involved with the industry. Many are aware that regardless of how much experience you have, the weather can change quickly, and the ocean can be very
unforgiving. We lost three fishermen from the DownEast area within the last 2 years. Tylar Michaud from Steuben was 18
years old when he went overboard from his fishing vessel Top Gun and on January 18"` the sinking of Sudden Impact
took the lives of Chet and Aaron Barrett from South Addison.
In both events, Marine Patrol along with fishermen and US Coast Guard responded and put into action their protocols for search and rescue efforts. The search plans for Tylar and Chet and Aaron were different and required different types of
resources and equipment. Marine Patrol did a great job working in both situations and putting best efforts into each search. Unfortunately, the outcome for both rescues was not the outcome anyone wanted.
In speaking with the fishing families about the safety and resources available, l tried to think of ways to help but not to
create more regulations or mandates. We all know everything comes down to funding availability and priorities. The intent
of this bill is to establish The Commercial Safety Fishing Fund designated to allow the Commissioner of the Department of Marine Resources, working with the Commercial Fishing Safety Council, to review and provide continue training for such things as diving or the purchase of technology like a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) that could do under water
investigations prior to divers being deployed or in lieu of divers in unsafe locations.
Being prepared for the unthinkable may not always be an option but having a fund is a tangible way to make sure the best
options are available for future incidents.
Thank you for your time today and I would be glad to answer any questions.
Sincerely,

Tiffany Strout State Representative
District 11 Addison, Beals, Columbia, Columbia Falls, Harrington, Jonesboro, Jonesport, Machias, Milbridge, Roque Bluffs, Whitneyville, Centerville Township, and North Washington (Part)

Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, Distinguished Members of the Marine
Resources Committee:
I am Will Tuell. I represent House District 10, which includes nearly 20 small communities in central and coastal Washington County. I am here today to wholeheartedly endorse LD 1708, a bill sponsored by my colleague and friend, Rep. Strout, who ably serves Western Washington County in the 132""
Legislature.
When you ride to and from Washington County together every week, you have a
chance to kick ideas, bills, and proposals around. Rep. Strout and I have had
many such opportunities during our white-knuckle trips to and from the Down East coast this winter and spring, and it was one such trip, I believe, that begat
this bill.
Chet and Aaron Barrett had lost their lives at sea while bringing their scallop boat
back home. I did not know the Barretts but have known several fishermen who
went overboard while out hauling traps or dragging for scallops. Downeast, it is an unspoken part of the lifestyle, a risk that goes with the job, one which
irrevocably devastates the lives of all who knew those lost.
We all remember the death of 18-year-old Tylar Michaud a couple years back.
Tylar had graduated from high school in June only to lose his life hauling traps
two months later. His great-aunt, the Honorable Joyce Maker, who once chaired
this committee, and who served on it with myself and Rep. Hepler, kept me
posted on the search and recovery effort. To say that was a harrowing ordeal for those involved would be an understatement. To say that Marine Patrol and the various agencies that assisted with the search did not go above and beyond
would also be wrong. -_
We have some incredible people on the water, whose mission it is to leave no
fisherman at sea. They truly and sincerely take every shipwreck personally and will do whatever they can to bring a loved one home, whether it be a rescue or,
all too often, a recovery.
So when Rep. Strout was, like many in the community, searching for answers, and ways to be of help, following the Barretts' shipwreck, I listened, and
suggested something I rarely ever suggest -- an after deadline bill.

House District 10

Rarely is there a true need for a late filed request, but we both agreed that the Barretts death, and the discussion that came from it, was a worthy case in point. That bill has been many things since it was first brought to Legislative Council, but the finished product, before you today as LD 1708, offers us an opportunity to do something proactive and positive for the commercial fishermen who put their
lives on the line every day. This bill sets up a fund for badly needed equipment and response efforts in the case of a shipwreck. In recognition of the fact that times are tight here at the
State House, it is designed in such a way that fishermen, the community at large, and anyone with a generous heart can donate funds to assist in timely search,
rescue, and recovery efforts.
The fishing community rallied around the Barrett family, stepped up in a big way to bring divers and equipment to the scene of the shipwreck. Many feel, and
rightly so, that the state should have such a fund already established -- a fund
which, if you'll pardon my editorializing against sites like GoFundMe -- does not
exploit grieving communities, families, and Mainers' goodwill.
By establishing this fund, and allowing people to donate to it, we are offering the entire coast - and beyond --- a way to help out in a time of crisis. Beyond that, we
are saying that it is our goal, as a state, to invest in the technology, resources,
and training needed to reduce the number of lives lost at sea, or, failing that, to recover those lost at sea as quickly as possible.
I urge you to join me in supporting LD 1708 and standing with the men and women who make a living at sea.
House District 10
